analysis_scope.sampling_notes: The checkout is shallow at depth 50 and therefore represents recent history only, although only five commits are visible. The repository is small: all 13 tracked files were inventoried, every text/source file was inspected, and the eight image assets were inventoried without pixel-level review.

stated_purpose: The README presents this as a USGS-themed earthquake-data visualization exercise using Leaflet to make recent seismic activity more meaningful to the public and government organizations.

observed_capabilities.statement: The browser application requests the USGS all-earthquakes-for-the-past-week GeoJSON feed and plots its point features on a Leaflet map.
Earthquake marker radius is derived from magnitude, while fill color is selected from depth thresholds based on the third GeoJSON coordinate.
Each marker opens a popup containing the reported place, magnitude, and depth.
The map uses OpenStreetMap tiles, starts centered over the contiguous United States, and exposes one earthquake overlay through a Leaflet layer control.

planned_work.statement: The historical assignment specification called for a legend and optionally proposed tectonic-plate data, additional base maps, independently switchable overlays, and expanded layer controls.
No current TODO, open issue, pull request, or recent commit evidence establishes that the historical optional enhancements remain planned work.

architecture.statement: The project is a build-free static web page consisting of one HTML entry point, one JavaScript implementation file, and minimal full-page map CSS.
At runtime the page loads Leaflet 1.6.0 and D3 v5 from third-party CDNs; D3 retrieves live USGS GeoJSON, Leaflet converts the features to circle markers, and OpenStreetMap supplies the base tiles.
There is no local server, backend, persistent data store, package-management layer, or build pipeline in the tracked tree.

accomplishments.statement: The implementation covers most of the assignment's core Part 1 behavior: fetching live earthquake data, plotting geographic markers, encoding magnitude and depth, and providing informational popups.
The repository includes a directly loadable map page and responsive full-viewport styling without requiring a compilation step.

gaps.statement: The required depth-color legend described by the historical assignment is not implemented, leaving the marker colors unexplained in the interface.
The optional tectonic-plate visualization and multiple base-map choices were not implemented.
The HTML references static/js/config.js, but that file is not tracked and the inspected implementation does not otherwise require an API key.
There are no tests, automated checks, dependency manifests, setup instructions, deployment artifacts, or runtime verification records.
The current README was reduced to background prose and no longer explains how to run the page, what was implemented, or which assignment requirements remain incomplete.

risks.statement: Successful rendering depends on several live third-party services and older CDN-loaded library versions, with no local dependency pinning beyond the Leaflet URL and integrity attribute.
The missing config.js reference will produce an avoidable failed resource request and may mislead maintainers into believing a secret-bearing configuration file is required.
Without tests or a documented verification procedure, changes in browser behavior, remote APIs, or GeoJSON data characteristics could break the visualization without detection.

The tracked VS Code workspace file contains repository-external relative paths referring to local Projects, Downloads, and other repositories, which is unnecessary environment-specific metadata in a public coursework repository.
No credential-named files were found in the tracked project tree, and the referenced config.js file is absent; no secret values were inspected.

suggested_next_actions.statement: Treat the repository as dormant coursework and archive it after owner review unless there is a concrete reason to preserve it as an actively usable example.
If retained as a reference, add concise run instructions and an implementation-status note, remove the stale config.js script reference and local workspace file, and add the missing depth legend.
Before presenting the project as functional, verify it in a browser against the current USGS feed and CDN dependencies and record that verification.

questions: Was this repository solely a completed coursework submission, or is it intended to remain a reusable Leaflet example?
Was the depth legend intentionally omitted, or was the submission unfinished?
Should the tracked VS Code workspace file and stale config.js reference be removed?
Is there a deployed copy or screenshot of the implemented map that could provide runtime evidence?

evidence.summary: Provided snapshot identifies a public repository on main, last pushed on 2022-08-06, with no description, open issues, or open pull requests.
Current README contains only the USGS-themed background and motivation for visualizing earthquake data.

The earlier Unit 15 homework specification requires an earthquake map with magnitude-sized and depth-colored markers, popups, and a legend; it describes tectonic plates and additional layers as optional Part 2 work.

Thirteen tracked files comprise README.md, index.html, eight instructional images, one CSS file, one JavaScript implementation, and one VS Code workspace file; no manifest, tests, workflow, deployment configuration, credential-named file, or config.js is present.
Static page creates a map container and loads Leaflet 1.6.0, D3 v5, a missing local config.js file, and logic.js.
Fetches the USGS all-week GeoJSON feed, creates magnitude-sized and depth-colored Leaflet circle markers with popups, and places them over OpenStreetMap with a layer control.
Removes page spacing and sizes the map, body, and HTML elements to the full viewport height.
VS Code workspace configuration references several repository-external relative paths associated with local Projects, Downloads, and other repositories.
All five visible commits occurred on 2022-08-06 and consist of uploaded files, directory relocation, and README reductions; no later maintenance history is present in the shallow checkout.

confidence.rationale: The complete small source tree, historical specification, and visible commit history support the implementation and dormancy conclusions. Confidence is limited because the live, internet-dependent visualization was not executed, there are no tests or deployment artifacts, and the checkout is shallow.

limitations: The live application was not executed, so successful rendering and current compatibility with external services are not proven.
The checkout is shallow at depth 50; history beyond that boundary would not be available, although only five commits are visible.
Image assets were inventoried but not reviewed pixel by pixel.
The supplied metadata does not independently establish whether GitHub's archive flag is enabled.
Suggested lifecycle and cleanup actions require owner review.
